raw_case_text:
A 31-year-old HIV-infected black African female presented with an 8-day history of painful swallowing, sore eyes, malaise and a worsening rash. She had been on antiretroviral (ARV) regimen of nevirapine (NVP) 400 mg daily, tenofovir 300 mg daily and lamivudine 300 mg daily for more than 4 years uneventfully. She was on no other medications and had not taken any other medication in the preceding 8 weeks. She had acquired HIV via heterosexual contact - the exact date of HIV infection was unknown. At the time of initiation of ARV therapy, her nadir CD4 cell count was 139 cells/mm 3 and her HIV RNA viral load at the time was unknown. Her last CD4 counts, done 31, 21 and 11 months before developing her current symptoms were 373, 356 and 387 cells/mm 3 respectively. The last HIV RNA viral load test, done 11 months prior to the onset of her symptoms showed an undetectable viral load.
She gave a history of forgetting to take her ARV medication for a day. The following day, 10 days before development of her symptoms she took 2 days equivalent of her ARVs in one day, in her own words "to make up for the missed dose".
On examination, she was normotensive and had a temperature of 38.8 C. She had conjunctivitis and hemorrhagic cheilitis but no involvement of the genital mucosa. She had epidermal necrosis involving predominantly her trunk and face and to a lesser extent palms, soles and extremities, totaling 10% of her body surface area, 3% of which was stripping. Initial laboratory studies showed normal blood count, except for an elevated eosinophil count of 0.70 x 10 9/L. The liver and renal function tests were normal. Her ARVs were stopped and her epidermal necrosis did not extend and eosinophil counts normalized. Over the next few days her skin condition improved and she was discharged 10 days later fully re-epithelialized with the exception of the lips, which were still eroded in areas. On review, 2 weeks after discharge, her skin had normalized except for residual hyperpigmentation. She was started on a single daily tablet of Odimune  , a fixed drug combination of tenofovir 300 mg, emtricitabine 200 mg and efavirenz 600 mg. On follow-up, 4 weeks later she was tolerating the new ARV regimen.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 31-year-old female presenting with painful swallowing, sore eyes, malaise, and a worsening rash for eight days.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with an 8-day history of painful swallowing, sore eyes, malaise, and a progressive rash. Ten days prior to symptom onset, she missed her daily medications for one day and subsequently took a double dose (two days' equivalent in a single day) to compensate. Her symptoms progressed to blistering and skin peeling involving the face, trunk, and extremities, prompting hospital admission.
subjective.past_medical_history: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection acquired via heterosexual contact; nadir CD4 cell count 139 cells/mm3; maintained on an antiretroviral therapy (ART) regimen of nevirapine 400 mg daily, tenofovir 300 mg daily, and lamivudine 300 mg daily for over 4 years uneventfully; serial CD4 counts 31, 21, and 11 months prior were 373, 356, and 387 cells/mm3, respectively, with undetectable viral load 11 months prior.
subjective.review_of_systems: Painful swallowing, sore eyes, malaise; denies genital mucosal symptoms. Home medications: Nevirapine 400 mg daily, tenofovir 300 mg daily, lamivudine 300 mg daily; no other medications in preceding 8 weeks.

objective.physical_examination: Temperature 38.8 °C, normotensive. Eyes: Conjunctivitis. Oropharynx: Hemorrhagic cheilitis; absence of genital mucosal involvement. Dermatologic: Epidermal necrosis involving predominantly the trunk and face, and to a lesser extent palms, soles, and extremities, totaling 10% of body surface area (BSA) with 3% stripping.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count: Normal, except for an elevated eosinophil count of 0.70 x 10^9/L. Liver and renal function tests: Normal.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) secondary to nevirapine toxicity / double-dosing in an HIV-infected patient on established antiretroviral therapy.
Plan & Outcome: Antiretroviral therapy was immediately discontinued. Epidermal necrosis arrested without further extension, and eosinophilia normalized. The patient was discharged after 10 days fully re-epithelialized except for residual lip erosions. At 2 weeks follow-up, skin had normalized with residual hyperpigmentation. Antiretroviral therapy was safely resumed with a single daily tablet of Odimune (fixed-dose combination of tenofovir 300 mg, emtricitabine 200 mg, and efavirenz 600 mg), which was well-tolerated at 4-week follow-up.
